description:
## Problem

Currently, meta-orchestration (planning initiatives and backlog items from a high-level vision) happens in external Claude Code conversations using the meta-orchestrator skill. This creates several problems:
1. The planning conversation context is lost after the session — only a static orchestration-summary.md survives
2. There's no way to resume or fork a planning conversation later when priorities change
3. Created initiatives and backlog items have no attribution back to the planning conversation that produced them
4. There's no way to validate that executed items align with the original planning intent
5. The planning UX is disconnected from the swarm-manager UI where the work is managed

This was discovered when planning the vrooli-events and notification-hub-greenfield initiatives. The planning produced 9 backlog items across 2 initiatives with detailed architecture decisions, but when items were executed, the agents didn't have sufficient context about WHY certain decisions were made, leading to drift.

## What Currently Exists

### Capture Button (reusable for entry point)
- `ui/src/components/capture/quick-capture-input.tsx` — textarea with Ctrl+Enter, image attachments, draft persistence in localStorage
- Flow: text → POST /api/v1/captures → auto-classify agent → triage UI in `capture-triage.tsx`
- This is the natural entry point for meta-orchestration: same input surface, new mode

### Chat/Conversation UI (reusable for orchestration conversation)
- `ui/src/components/backlog/clarification-panel.tsx` — draggable FloatingPanel with full chat UX
- `ui/src/components/backlog/clarification-messages.tsx` — message thread renderer with markdown + images
- Zustand store for state management, 3-second polling for agent responses, 90-second staleness warning
- Draft persistence, attachment handling, action buttons with confirmation
- This is production-ready for multi-turn conversations and can be adapted for meta-orchestration

### Agent Identity and Attribution (reusable for linking)
- `api/internal/identity/` — X-Agent-Identity-Token header with Provenance (type, run_id, task_id, profile_key)
- `api/internal/agentactivity/` — tracks owner_type, purpose, interaction_type, metadata including skill_id
- Environment variables with VROOLI_ prefix passed via CreateRunRequest.environment
- Currently uses VROOLI_SPAWN_SOURCE for backlog attribution

### Agent-Manager Integration (reusable for spawning)
- SpawnBacklog() + ContinueRun() for multi-turn agent conversations
- Run state polling with status tracking
- Prompt catalog for skill-based agent initialization

## Vision

The capture button becomes a dual-mode entry point:
- **Quick capture** (existing): fire-and-forget text → classification → suggested items
- **Meta-orchestration** (new): opens a conversation panel → agent with meta-orchestrator skill → iterative planning → creates initiatives + items with full attribution

Meta-orchestration runs become first-class entities:
- Each has a unique ID and is stored persistently
- The full conversation (all turns) is preserved and resumable
- Created initiatives and backlog items carry a `meta_orchestration_id` linking back
- The UI shows which orchestration session produced which items
- You can resume a session later to review progress, adjust priorities, or plan follow-up work

## Key Design Decisions to Workshop
- How meta-orchestration sessions are stored (new JSON file? new SQLite table? folder structure?)
- How the capture button mode switch works in the UI (toggle? dropdown? auto-detect from input length?)
- How conversation continuity works (ContinueRun to same agent? New agent with full history injected?)
- Whether meta-orchestration should have its own page in the UI or live within the existing captures/backlog pages
- How the resume/fork UX works (load conversation, show what was created, allow follow-up)
- What metadata to attach to created items (just the orchestration ID? or richer context like decision rationale?)
name: meta-orchestration-native-sessions
title: Make Meta-Orchestration A First Class Swarm Manager Feature With Conversation Persistence And Attribution
